draft.title: Principal Hindu beliefs
card: Many Hindus believe in Brahman, the ultimate reality behind everything that exists. Hindus understand and worship Brahman in many ways, including through many gods and goddesses.
Samsara is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth. Many Hindus believe the soul (atman) is reborn again and again.
Karma is the principle that actions have results. A person's actions shape the conditions of their future life in samsara.
Moksha is liberation from samsara. Many Hindus see it as the highest goal, where the soul is freed from the cycle of rebirth.
draft.remember: Karma shapes rebirth in samsara, and moksha is release from that cycle.

a.q: In Hindu belief, what is moksha?
opts: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
The results of a person's actions
The ultimate reality behind all things
The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
a.why: Moksha is freedom from samsara, so the soul is no longer reborn. The cycle itself is samsara, which is the most tempting wrong option because the two ideas are closely linked.
a.clue: Think of the goal that ends the cycle.

b.q: Dev believes his kind and honest actions will lead to a better future life. Which Hindu belief is he relying on?
opts: Moksha ending the cycle of rebirth
Samsara as a goal to be reached
b.why: Dev links his actions to the conditions of a future life. That is karma shaping rebirth in samsara. Moksha is wrong because it is release from rebirth, not a better rebirth.
b.clue: Which belief connects actions to future lives?

a.best: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
